findings.title: Add/remove members reads group_id but the route supplies id
findings.body: add_members and remove_member both do Group.find(params.require(:group_id)). The new routes are member routes on resources :groups (DELETE/PUT /admin/groups/:id/members), so Rails populates params[:id], not params[:group_id]. The client only puts the id in the path (/admin/groups/:id/members.json) and sends usernames or user_id in the body. params.require(:group_id) therefore raises ParameterMissing and every add or remove from the admin UI returns 400. Controller specs hide this by passing group_id directly and never hitting the router.

findings.title: Creating a group drops alias_level
findings.body: create only assigns name and visible. The admin form shows the alias-level combo for new groups, and Group#asJSON posts alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but the action never reads it. A group created with anything other than the default alias level (for example everyone / 99) is saved as the default, and the choice is silently lost. update does apply alias_level, so the field only works after the group already exists.

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: totalPages is Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (50 members, limit 50) that is 2 instead of 1. showingLast stays false on the real last page, so Next is enabled. next then sets offset to user_count and findMembers loads an empty extra page. Use ceil(user_count / limit), and treat a zero count as zero pages.

findings.title: Remove control ignores automatic groups
findings.body: The member row is an itemView whose context is the user, not the group, so {{#unless automatic}} does not see the group's automatic flag. The flag is always falsy on the user, so the remove link is rendered for automatic groups (trust levels, staff, and so on). The server rejects those deletes with 422, and removeMember never surfaces the error, so the confirm dialog appears to succeed and the member stays. The add-members block in group.hbs correctly hides itself; this row does not.

findings.title: Removing the last member on a page leaves a blank page
findings.body: removeMember reloads with the current offset and does not move back a page when that page becomes empty. The members action echoes the requested offset and does not clamp it to the new total. After deleting the last user on a page, the response has members: [] while offset is still past the new user_count. The client stores that offset, so the admin stays on a blank page until they click Previous. findMembers only clamps offset against the stale user_count from before the delete.

findings.title: Members limit and offset are not bounded
findings.body: limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i and offset is params[:offset].to_i with no upper or lower bound, on a public endpoint that now paginates every group including large automatic ones. A caller can pass limit of millions or a negative limit/offset. limit(0) is also echoed back to the admin client, which then divides user_count by that limit and produces Infinity/NaN page numbers. Clamp limit to a small positive maximum (and offset to >= 0) before querying.

findings.title: GET group members response shape changed without a compatibility path
findings.body: GET /groups/:id/members used to render a JSON array of users via GroupUserSerializer. It now returns {members, meta}. Any plugin, theme, or external client that still treats the body as an array will break. The in-repo templates were updated, but nothing in this PR versions the endpoint or keeps the old array format.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove spec uses PUT and never hits the route
findings.body: The example "cannot remove members from automatic groups" calls xhr :put, :remove_member, while the route is DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members and the success example correctly uses :delete. Controller specs invoke the action by name and inject group_id, so this never checks routing or that params[:id] is what the action reads. That is why the group_id vs :id mismatch is untested. The members action's new {members, meta} contract also has no spec.
